args.query: how do I build a golden test set to measure RAG retrieval quality, and which metrics should I track?

events.response_text:
Compiled research from Wren (3 pages):
[S1] Golden Datasets: How to build, size and maintain the labeled test set behind your evals, including when synthetic data helps and when it misleads. Metric definitions live in rag-retrieval-metrics.
[S2] Eval Strategy Overview: How to stand up evals for an LLM app: start from real failures, layer cheap checks under expensive ones, and keep a human in the loop for calibration. Measure retrieval with recall@k against a labeled set, then measure generation separately on cases where retrieval succeeded.
[S3] RAG Retrieval Metrics: Which numbers to track for the retrieval half of a RAG system, how to compute them on a small labeled set, and what usually moves them. Evaluate retrieval first, using a labeled set of queries where you know which documents or chunks are relevant.
Sources: golden-datasets.md, eval-strategy-overview.md, rag-retrieval-metrics.md

Feedback saved for sim_390a483de3e2 (useful, 5/5). Wren's reputation: 3.00 -> 3.09 of 5.
